page.layout: One column of running text, with marginal notes in the right margin. The printed page number and running head are at the top. Below the text there is a gathering signature at the left.

main_text.p: cliti, civibus non minus pugnandum est pro legibus, quàm pro mœnibus: quòd absq; mœnibus, nō autem absq; legibus incolumis esse possit civitas: non minus religiosè elaborandum, ut salutaria edicta de pietatis exercitijs, de fuga vitiorū, de disciplina & progymnasmatis virtutum, locum habeant in Ecclesia, quæ sanctorum ἁγίων κοινωνία[?] id est, societas est.
main_text.head: VERSVS IX.

p.i: Quis scit si convertatur, et pœniteat Deum, avertaturq; à furore iræ suæ: & non peribimus?

main_text.p: Hæc est altera pars regij edicti, in qua agitur περὶ τῶν πιστῶν[?] ἢ[?] ἐλπιζομένων, id est, de iis quæ credenda & sperānda essent conversis ad Deum.

Poterant Niniuitæ dicere: Cur ad ieiunium[illegible, ~6 letters], ad saccum, ad supplicationes, denique ad conversionem ipsis factis contestandam nos vocas? Respondetur: Quia spes est, Deum pro infinita sua clementia nobis parsurum esse, si resipiscamus.superiorum. Eodem sane modo Dominus per Ieremiam Israelitis resipiscentibus pollicetur veniam. Si reversus fueris Israel, dixit Ieho-vah,

page.notes: Greek marginal note at the line "Poterant Niniuitæ" is too faint to read reliably; it is marked illegible. The Greek phrase in the sentence beginning "Hæc est altera pars" and the Greek word before "id est" in the first paragraph are doubtful and carry [?]. The text "ἐλπιζομένων" is read from the scan with some uncertainty. The word "superiorum." is an italic marginal reference. The printed "fta" in "edicta" stands for the ligature "ct". The printed "f" for long s has been written as "s" throughout. The signature "t 4" is at the foot of the page.
